title: EU tech chief says bloc 'well equipped' to fend off rogue AI risk
source_used: The News International (Reuters story relayed); Cryptopolitan for context
key_facts: EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen said on Friday 9 Oct 2026 that Europe is 'well equipped' to deal with rogue AI agents.
She said the AI Act, adopted by the bloc two years ago, 'covers the whole life cycle' of advanced models.
The AI Act regulates AI by risk level.
She said regulators are giving guidance on validating models and will use input from a 60-member panel of scientific experts.
The European Commission sent information requests in late August to several AI companies on risk mitigation, compliance and intellectual property.
She said the most capable models on the market are from the United States and China.
She said EU governments are now discussing funding for 2028-2034 and a possible digital tax that would mainly hit large US tech companies.
quote_evidence: We see that the safety and security of very capable models is a very hot topic internationally and we in Europe are well equipped for that.
We have our AI Act in place and the AI Act covers the whole life cycle of these models.
The EU has the first law in the world that addresses systemic risk from AI, and we need state-of-the-art scientific input.
why_it_matters_hint: The EU's top tech official says the existing AI law is enough to handle losing control of AI agents; it is her own assessment.
